chapter.title: The Blue Planet
chapter.tagline: Reflections from space orbit: Shubhanshu Shukla, the International Space Station, and protecting our one shared home
chapter.overview: Inspired by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla's historic mission to the International Space Station, students view Earth from orbital altitude. They witness that borders, states, and fences do not exist from orbit—our planet is a radiant blue marble cushioned by a thin blue atmosphere, requiring collective human care.

sections.title: Looking Down from Space: An Astronaut's Perspective
sections.subtitle: Shubhanshu Shukla's historic message to the nation from orbit

storyNarrative.dialogue: When you look at Earth from the cupola of the Space Station, the first thought that hits you is that the Earth is completely ONE! No borders, no state lines, no divides exist. We are all passengers on one ship!

concept.heading: The Overview Effect
concept.keyRule: The cognitive shift experienced by astronauts seeing Earth from space as a fragile, borderless sphere suspended in the cosmic void.

questions.prompt: What striking feature does an astronaut notice about national borders when viewing Earth from space?
options: No borders or boundaries are visible from space
Borders look like high stone walls
Borders are marked by deep rivers
questions.correctAnswer: No borders or boundaries are visible from space
questions.hint: Borders are human concepts, not natural features.

sections.title: The Fragile Blue Atmosphere & Microgravity
sections.subtitle: How a paper-thin blanket of air shields life on Earth

storyNarrative.dialogue: Captain Shukla, why does the atmosphere look so thin like a glowing blue ribbon on the edge of the planet? Does it protect us from the vacuum of space?

concept.heading: Atmospheric Shielding & Life Support
concept.keyRule: Earth's atmosphere shields surface organisms from solar cosmic radiation, burns incoming meteors, and maintains temperatures suitable for liquid water.

options: It blocks harmful cosmic radiation and traps breathable oxygen

sections.title: Stewards of Spaceship Earth: Our Shared Future
sections.subtitle: Ecological responsibility and global citizenship

storyNarrative.dialogue: In space, if your oxygen recycler breaks or your water leaks, everyone must work together to fix it. Earth is our grand spaceship—we cannot fly away to another planet; we must protect this one!

concept.heading: Planetary Environmental Stewardship
concept.keyRule: Conservation of oceans, soil, forests, and atmosphere is the shared, non-negotiable responsibility of every nation and human being.

questions.prompt: Why is planet Earth compared to a spaceship?
options: It has jet engines on the bottom
It travels through space with finite resources that all crew members must protect
It is made of metal and glass
It can travel at the speed of light
